title: Half-Life 2
wiki_lead:
Half-Life 2 is a 2004 first-person shooter (FPS) game developed and published by Valve Corporation. It was published for Windows on November 16, 2004, on Valve's digital distribution service, Steam. Like the original Half-Life (1998), Half-Life 2 combines combat, puzzles and storytelling, and adds features such as vehicles and physics-based gameplay. The player controls Gordon Freeman, who joins a resistance effort to liberate Earth from the alien Combine empire.
Valve developed Half-Life 2 using its Source game engine, developed simultaneously. Development lasted five years and cost US $40 million. Valve's president, Gabe Newell, set his team the goal of redefining the FPS genre. They integrated the Havok physics engine, which simulates real-world physics, to reinforce the sense of presence and create new gameplay. They also developed the characterization, with more detailed character models and animations.
Valve announced Half-Life 2 at E3 2003 with a release date of September of that year. They failed to meet the release date, leading to fan backlash. In October, an unfinished version leaked online, damaging morale and leading to further backlash.
Half-Life 2 received acclaim and won 39 Game of the Year. Like its predecessor, it has been cited as one of the most influential FPS games and among the greatest video games. It was ported to Xbox, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, macOS and Linux. By 2011, it had sold 12 million copies. Half-Life 2 was followed by the free extra level Lost Coast (2005) and the episodic sequels Episode One (2006) and Episode Two (2007). In 2020, after canceling Episode Three and several further Half-Life projects, Valve released a prequel, Half-Life: Alyx.

Gameplay

Like the original Half-Life (1998), Half-Life 2 is a single-player first-person shooter (FPS) in which the player controls Gordon Freeman. It features combat, exploration, jumping challenges, and puzzle-solving, and narrative elements conveyed through scripted sequences. Weapons include a pistol, submachine gun, shotgun, and the powerful Combine pulse rifle. With the bugbait item, enemy antlions become allies and can be called to the player or sent to attack enemies.
Half-Life 2 introduces detailed physics simulation. With the new gravity gun, players can repel objects or pull them from a distance. For example, objects can be fired at enemies, held as shields, or placed to reach new areas, and enemy grenades can be caught and thrown back. The player must also use physics to solve puzzles. Half-Life 2 also adds sections in which the player controls an airboat and a dune buggy.

After the alien invasion at the Black Mesa Research Facility, a multidimensional alien empire known as the Combine has conquered Earth. grok_lead: Half-Life 2 is a first-person shooter video game developed and published by Valve Corporation. Released on November 16, 2004, for Microsoft Windows, it serves as the direct sequel to the 1998 game Half-Life and continues the story of silent protagonist Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist who battles the invading alien Combine empire. Set in the dystopian, occupied metropolis of City 17 following Earth's surrender in the Seven Hour War, the game follows Freeman as he awakens from stasis and allies with resistance fighter Alyx Vance to lead a human uprising against the Combine's totalitarian regime. Powered by Valve's proprietary Source engine, Half-Life 2 introduced groundbreaking features including realistic physics simulation via the integrated Havok engine, advanced NPC artificial intelligence, and seamless narrative integration without cutscenes, all contributing to its immersive world-building and exhilarating combat. Critically acclaimed upon release, Half-Life 2 holds a Metacritic score of 96 out of 100 based on 81 reviews, earning it designations as Game of the Year from over 35 organizations and Game of the Decade honors from outlets like IGN and the Spike Video Game Awards. Commercially successful, it sold 1.7 million retail copies worldwide in its first two months and reached 6.5 million boxed units by 2008, with total PC ownership estimated at over 10 million by 2017. The title played a pivotal role in establishing Steam as the dominant digital distribution platform for PC gaming, as it was the first major release requiring the serviceâeven for retail purchasersâdriving millions of new account creations despite initial backlash over its mandatory authentication and early technical issues. Expanded through two episodic sequels, Half-Life 2: Episode One (2006) and Episode Two (2007), and later ports to platforms like Xbox, PlayStation 3, macOS, Linux, and Android, the game received a 20th anniversary update in 2024 that bundled the episodes, added developer commentary and Steam Workshop support, and included quality-of-life improvements. It has influenced countless titles in the genre with its emphasis on environmental storytelling and player agency.
